LLM_description:
Situation:
Severe flooding has disrupted ground lines of communication in the region. Supply Depot Alpha and Supply Depot Bravo remain operational and are serving as primary staging nodes. Supported sites include FOB North, Field Hospital Lima, IDP Camp Sierra, and Community Shelter West. Multiple road corridors are partially open but subject to washouts, debris, and intermittent security incidents. Some lanes require route clearance and armed escorts before any movement can depart, and weather is expected to deteriorate after the current operational period.

Mission:
Deliver life-sustaining commodities (water, staple rations, and medical items) from the depots to the supported sites within the current operational period, minimizing total operational cost while preserving force protection. Total cost comprises transport costs, shortage penalties for unmet demand, per-vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs. Shortfalls are acceptable only where required by constraints, and should be minimized and focused away from critical-care demands.

Execution/Concept:
- Supply and demand:
  - Shipments may originate from either depot to any supported site. Shipments can be split across depots and commodities as required.
  - Outbound flows from each depot cannot exceed available stock by item.
  - Unmet demand at a site is captured as controlled shortfall with an associated penalty; this represents deferral or substitution of deliveries where risk or access prohibits full fulfillment.
- Mobility and capacity:
  - Vehicles are discrete assets with fixed payload capacity measured in volumetric terms; each commodity consumes capacity according to its volume per unit.
  - Total vehicles used across all routes is capped by fleet availability for the period.
  - Loads per route cannot exceed the carrying capacity implied by the number of vehicles assigned to that route.
- Route activation and risk:
  - A route from a depot to a supported site is considered inactive until deliberately opened. Activating any route (sending one or more vehicles) incurs a fixed Risk Cost for that lane that represents escorts, clearance teams, and security overhead. This fixed Risk Cost is charged once per active route per period regardless of the number of vehicles assigned to it.
  - Vehicles may only be dispatched on routes that have been activated; if a lane is not activated, no vehicles may be sent.
- Cost-minimizing approach:
  - Select which depot-to-site lanes to activate by comparing the fixed risk/security overhead against expected transport cost savings and demand priorities.
  - Consolidate loads to reduce the number of activated routes and escort burdens without violating capacity or depot availability.
  - Allocate flows to meet the highest-priority medical and water demands first, using shortage penalties to guide trade-offs when access or capacity is constrained.
  - Favor safer, more reliable corridors when risk-adjusted costs are comparable to hazardous alternatives.
- Coordination:
  - Route clearance elements and security escorts synchronize with convoy departures from both depots.
  - Distribution teams at supported sites will stage offloading and onward movement to reduce dwell time on unsecured routes.
  - Updates to route status will trigger re-optimization of lane activation and vehicle allocation within the operational period.
